proof.text: Apply the existing source-library rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange_fac_app to d. Its four factors are precisely W(gamma_et), respectively the exact W localization factor, Q(d), gamma_proet, and the inverse V localization factor. The homotopy composition isomorphisms of identity composite identifications are identities. Componentwise extensionality therefore gives graphMateLeft = graphMateRight for every bounded-below representative, including noninjective ones. This is the defining localization factorization of the canonical base-change map.

For the left transpose, expand homEquiv.symm as L(-) followed by the derived counit. Use fixedComparisonDirectImageMatePlus_counit, cancel only the isomorphism a, and move gamma_et through a inverse by naturality. The existing normalized derivedPlus_counit_app_fac then gives exactly a inverse followed by V of the localized ordinary etale counit. For the right transpose, move the inverse V localization factor through the derived counit by naturality, and apply the primed derivedPlus_counit_app_fac. This gives precisely the stated pro-etale counit expression. The representative equality of the preceding step, transported through the same Hom equivalence, identifies these two expressions.

Take the sheaf graph square for the specified compactification and its uniquely specified pro-etale graph map. Apply mapHomotopyCategoryPlus to the equality of natural transformations; this operation preserves composition and whiskering, so the square holds on all bounded-below homotopy representatives. The exact-functor composition and natural-isomorphism factorization formulas compute the derived sigma and open comparison o on those representatives. The localization preimage defining each graph transformation has exactly graphMateRepresentativeGraph as its whiskering with Qh.

proof.text: Substitute those factorization equations into the left graph endpoint. The localized sheaf square and naturality of gamma_proet at the actual open comparison identify it with the displayed middle expression. Substitute graphMateRight = graphMateLeft, then use naturality of b at the inverse open-extension localization factor; the result is the whiskering of the right graph endpoint. Fully faithful precomposition with Qh detects equality of the descended endpoints. Only exact-functor localization isomorphisms are canceled; neither gamma nor comparison of injectives is assumed invertible.

The base is the Q106 node C, which is identical to live and side-live, still unsplit there, and has no repair note. The delivery changes only the final sentence of the statement. It now says the first display is natural in complexes P (its source Q(p_*P) does not descend), while the graph chain is an identity on D^+(U_et,A). This is correct and not a weakening: every display and hypothesis is unchanged, and the parent varying-ring-graph-summand step 2 uses the chain only at a bounded K. Dropping def-pc-fibre-product from stmt_deps is correct. I recomputed every step. Step 2: the 0FND formula with s=t=f=id gives e(γ_B)=Q(ε^0_B), which is the counit identity (*). On the pro-étale side the cocone at id is Q(u_*i_B); def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations defines the adjunction as this 0FND bijection, and canonical-mate cites it for both pairs. Step 3: the canonical-mate normalization (finite Λ, qcqs, D^+), naturality of a^{-1}, then (*). Step 4: the mate of α=a^{-1} with L_1=l, L_2=L, G=W, H=V gives ε^0L(d)=V(ε^0)a^{-1}; the two transposes are equal, and the Hom bijection is injective. Step 5: every hypothesis of the graph-sheaf-square node is present; the square holds degreewise, then naturality of γ at o_K. Step 6 is elementary. Step 7: e_Σ! and j_! are exact and o identifies the pro-étale target, so localization-universal-property (2)/(3) descends the outer terms. Small cases p=id, e=id, U=∅ and non-injective P all check. No SGA, no cycle. I accept the declared tool_uses (generic exactness, derived-adjunction, localization and normalization tools). Advisory: lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-mate-model (reviewed pass) is a generic form of the first clause. Its adjunction has the same counit identity (*), so the two adjunctions coincide. The report's search missed it, but re-deriving the clause from 0FND is correct and about as long, so it is not a fault. Review in review.md.
